title: Reconcile tenant graph glitches causing duplicate billing
creator: Priya Anand
description:
Summary:

We are seeing a class of multi-tenant attribution errors that result in duplicate billing for the same token usage. Root cause appears to be stale/ambiguous tenant graph state in the attribution service after sub-account merges and key retirement flows. In several incidents monitored over the last month customers reported 2x token usage charges and we see the billing pipeline counting the same request under two tenant IDs (parent + merged-child).

Why this matters:
- Direct customer impact: double charges, invoice disputes, revenue reconciliation churn.
- Operational: rate limiter and quota enforcement misfires (requests get counted against both workspaces causing unexpected throttling).

Observed evidence:
- Billing dashboard spike on 2026-03-03 at 03:14 UTC for tenant 'acme-inc' correlating to token XXXXXX-abc.
- Trace IDs where attribution_service returned two owner entries (owner_id and legacy_owner_id) for same request: trace 3f2a7b5c and 9c4d2e1a.
- Cache TTLs for tenant-graph entries are 10m; merges and key-rotation events currently publish an event but attribution service's subscriber logic misses some merge events during high load windows.

Hypothesis:
The attribution service relies on an in-memory cached view of the tenant graph and token->tenant mappings. When a subaccount is merged into a parent (or a token is rotated/retired), we do not synchronously invalidate or refresh the cached mapping for tokens associated with the merged account, so historical mappings and new authoritative mappings coexist. Some code paths perform a shallow merge of owners which ends up emitting billing rows for both owner IDs.
steps_to_reproduce: Create org A with workspace W-child (subaccount) and parent org A-root
Issue API token T1 scoped to W-child and generate steady traffic for 24h
Use admin flow to merge W-child into A-root (merge event published) and retire T1; issue new token T2 for A-root
Continue sending requests using T1 or T2 during and after merge window
Observe billing pipeline: rows show usage attributed to both W-child and A-root for overlapping time ranges (billing-raw table)
Run attribution_service logs filtered by token T1/T2 and observe duplicate owner resolution path returning both IDs
impact: Duplicate billing for affected customers, quota enforcement anomalies, increased invoice disputes and support load.
debugging_notes: Checked attribution_service metrics: subscriber lag spikes coinciding with high merge volume. Found two code paths: fast-path reads from local cache and fallback that hits tenant-graph service; under race conditions both populate billing metadata. The merge event handler currently enqueues a cache-refresh job but does not block attribution reads, so transient dual-state is expected. Example log snippet: 'attribution:resolve token=xxxxx returned owners=[W-child,A-root]'.
proposed_fix: 1) Add atomic token owner canonicalization: attribution_service must consult authoritative token->tenant store (token_registry) as single source-of-truth when merge/rotation events are recent. 2) Implement immediate cache invalidation for token entries on merge/key-rotation events and guarantee event delivery with an ack/retry loop. 3) Add a conservative de-duplication step in billing pipeline that collapses duplicate owner events within a 2-minute window and flags them for human review. 4) Backfill job to reconcile historical duplicate rows for the window 2026-02-15..2026-03-10 (heuristic: same trace/request id with two owners).
implementation_tasks: Add token_registry read path to attribution_service and make it the authoritative lookup for owner resolution
Change merge/key-rotation event handler to synchronously invalidate cache entries for affected tokens (feature-flagged)
Add integration test: simulate merge + rotation concurrency and assert billing rows have single owner
Implement de-duplication stage in billing ETL and add metric for deduped rows
Write backfill pipeline to correct already-duplicated billing rows and generate a reconciliation report
Add migration script to re-run attribution for affected date ranges in billing DB (dry-run first)
Create canary release behind feature flag and deploy to staging then a single low-impact production tenant before global rollout
test_plan: Unit tests for attribution_service token lookup fallback and cache invalidation
E2E scenario: merge flow under synthetic load with token churn; assert no duplicate billing rows
Load test the event-delivery path to ensure ack/retry does not add unacceptable latency
Manual validation: run backfill dry-run and compare diff report with expected duplicates
Customer-facing validation: pick 2 affected customers and verify statement adjustments are correct after backfill
rollout_plan: Gate the changes behind 'attr-canonicalization' feature flag. Deploy to staging, run the synthetic E2E merge test, then enable for 1% of production tenants for 24h while monitoring dedupe metrics and invoice delta. If stable, ramp to 100% over 48h. Backfill will run as a separate job; run dry-run first, then schedule off-peak full run with notification to billing ops.
rollback_plan: Feature flag off will revert to current behavior. For in-flight backfills, preserve snapshots and have a rollback script to restore pre-backfill rows from snapshots. If dedupe introduces under-counting, re-run attribution pipeline in audit mode for affected windows.
observability: Add metrics: attribution.duplicate_owner_count, attribution.cache_invalidation_failures, billing.deduped_rows. Add tracing tag 'owner_canonicalized=true/false'. Dashboard: 'Billing Attribution Health' with alert if duplicate_owner_count > 0 for >15m.
notes: PM input (2026-03-11): prioritize backfill and customer notifications before full rollout.
Support: Escalation queue has 7 open tickets referencing overcharges; CFO flagged as high priority.
Trade-offs: synchronous invalidation adds latency to merge flow; mitigated by doing only targeted token invalidations and keeping feature behind flag.
acceptance_criteria: No new duplicate billing rows in production for 48h post-ramp (monitor via metric)
Backfill dry-run matches expected duplicates and full run corrects counts for >95% of identified rows
Integration and E2E tests pass in CI and staging
Customer-facing invoice adjustments posted for reconciled overcharges and billing ops sign-off
